name: Household privacy rights by state
description: Official-source findings for all 51 jurisdictions. Each supported field has an exact retained quote. Unresolved cells do not imply that a law or right is absent.
scope: All 50 states and DC. Source-supported consumer privacy provisions, operative and future dates, agency rules and reviewed narrow protections. Unresolved fields do not establish that a right is absent.
update_policy: Recheck official routes quarterly. Record corrections in the changelog. Legal fields require separate statutory review.

columns.label: Other protection established by this review

changelog.change: Initial source audit. Program contact routes and legal eligibility remain separate.
Reviewed all 51 jurisdiction entries. Added current primary-source rights, agent rules, dated phases and explicit limits. Unknown cells are not findings of no protection.

rows.law: Alabama Personal Data Protection Act. Enacted rights begin May 1, 2027.
rows.citation: Alabama Code chapter 8-44; Act 2026-552.
rows.effective_date: May 1, 2027. Enacted future law.
rows.right_to_delete: Covered right to delete personal data concerning the consumer. Statutory exceptions and compliance alternatives apply. This right begins May 1, 2027.
rows.opt_out_sale_sharing: Covered opt-outs for targeted advertising, sale and qualifying profiling. The profiling provision specifies solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects. These rights begin May 1, 2027.
rows.global_privacy_signal: Not determined within the reviewed source scope.
rows.authorized_agent: The enacted section permits a known child's parent or legal guardian, or a consumer's guardian or conservator, to exercise the listed opt-outs. This finding does not establish a general adult-agent procedure. The provision begins May 1, 2027.
rows.agent_proof: The enacted provision requires commercially reasonable authentication of consumer requests and permits necessary additional information. Its opt-out fraud qualification is separate. The provision begins May 1, 2027.
rows.publicly_available_exemption: The enacted definition includes specified government records, widely distributed media and information the controller reasonably believes the consumer made public. Consumer-rights provisions begin May 1, 2027.

rows.state_deletion_platform: Not determined within the reviewed source scope.

rows.law: California Consumer Privacy Act, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act.
rows.citation: California Civil Code sections 1798.100 through 1798.199.100; 11 CCR section 7063 for the cited agent rule.
rows.effective_date: January 1, 2023 for CPRA amendments. This is not the CCPA original enactment date.
rows.right_to_delete: Covered right to request deletion of personal information, subject to CCPA exceptions and verification requirements.
rows.opt_out_sale_sharing: Covered opt-out of sale and sharing for cross-context behavioral advertising.
rows.global_privacy_signal: Covered businesses must honor qualifying opt-out preference signals
rows.authorized_agent: California regulations permit an authorized agent to submit deletion, correction and knowledge requests under section 7063. Other request types have their own rules.
rows.agent_proof: For deletion, correction and knowledge requests, the business may require signed permission and direct consumer identity verification or direct confirmation of permission. The power-of-attorney exception applies, but a business cannot require a power of attorney merely to use an agent.
rows.publicly_available_exemption: Personal information excludes publicly available information
rows.broker_registry: CalPrivacy publishes an annual Data Broker Registry. The current registry covers businesses reporting 2025 activities. The dynamic page display does not establish an independently verified broker count.
rows.state_deletion_platform: DROP accepts eligible California residents' broker-deletion requests. Broker processing began August 1, 2026. Brokers must access it at least every 45 days, and status updates can take up to 90 days.
rows.narrow_protection: Not determined within the reviewed source scope.

rows.law: Colorado Privacy Act.
rows.citation: Colorado Revised Statutes sections 6-1-1301 through 6-1-1314.
rows.effective_date: July 1, 2023. The universal opt-out requirement began July 1, 2024.
rows.right_to_delete: Covered right to delete personal data concerning the consumer. Statutory exceptions and compliance alternatives apply.
rows.opt_out_sale_sharing: Covered opt-outs for targeted advertising, sale and qualifying profiling. The statutory profiling definition and exceptions apply.
rows.global_privacy_signal: Covered controllers must honor qualifying opt-out mechanisms or signals beginning July 1, 2024. Technical, consent and statutory conditions apply.
rows.authorized_agent: A consumer may designate another person to exercise the statutory opt-outs. This finding does not establish an agent right to exercise every consumer request.
rows.agent_proof: The controller must be able to verify or authenticate identity and the agent's authority with commercially reasonable effort.
rows.publicly_available_exemption: Personal data excludes publicly available information. The definition includes specified government records and information the controller reasonably believes the consumer made public.

rows.law: Indiana Consumer Data Protection Act.
rows.citation: Indiana Code article 24-15, as described in the Attorney General's consumer guide.
rows.effective_date: January 1, 2026.
rows.right_to_delete: Covered right to delete personal data provided by or obtained about the consumer. Statutory exceptions and compliance alternatives apply.
rows.opt_out_sale_sharing: Covered opt-outs for targeted advertising, sale and qualifying profiling. The statutory profiling definition and exceptions apply.

rows.authorized_agent: The Attorney General explains that exercising another adult's rights requires a power of attorney or other legal authorization. The guidance separately recognizes rights for a child.

rows.law: Vermont Data Privacy and Online Surveillance Act. Enacted consumer rights begin January 1, 2028.

rows.publicly_available_exemption: The future definition includes public sources but excludes specified biometrics, assembled consumer profiles, related inferences, mixed personal-data profiles and other listed material. The consumer-rights provisions begin January 1, 2028.
